blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: Every drain below the street sewer's flow line, like your floor drain, a basement bathroom, or a laundry line, normally relies on gravity to reach the sewer. An overhead sewer system reroutes those drains into a sump pit instead. An [ejector pump](/elmhurst/ejector-pump) lifts that wastewater up to a line above flood level, where a check valve keeps it from flowing back down. From there, gravity carries it the rest of the way to the street sewer, the same as every drain upstairs.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewer Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: We flooded in 2013. Will an overhead sewer stop it?
items.preview: If it was a sewer backup, yes.
items.answer: If water came up through the floor drain, yes. If it seeped through the walls, that's groundwater, which needs a sump pump or waterproofing.

items.q: Does an overhead sewer work during a power outage?
items.answer: The ejector pump needs power. A battery backup or generator keeps it running, and the basement fixtures shouldn't be used during an outage.
Yes. It drains to the new pit with the rest of the basement.

items.q: How long does a conversion take?
items.answer: Usually a few days, depending on layout and finishes.

items.q: Is an overhead sewer worth it in a newer Elmhurst home?
items.preview: If it has backed up, it can be.
items.answer: If it has backed up before, yes. In 2013, homes old and new were damaged.

items.q: How much does an overhead sewer cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on your basement. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on sewer depth, layout, fixtures and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
